title: Supreme Court Strikes Down IEEPA Tariffs: What Importers Need to Know Now
date_evidence: February 20, 2026 | The U.S. Supreme Court on February 20, 2026, held that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) does not authorize the president to impose tariffs.
key_claim: The Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026; within hours the administration imposed a Section 122 surcharge (10 percent, 15 percent cap, 150 days) and launched Section 301 investigations as replacements.
frame_summary: The United States is rerouting its tariff weapon from the invalidated IEEPA route into Section 122 and Section 301, keeping coercive trade pressure intact through other statutory tools.
signals_supported: US tariff regime after the IEEPA ruling
verbatim_quote: Within hours after the decision was released, President Donald Trump announced the imposition of 10 percent global tariffs under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974

title: Section 301'ing the World (or 99.4% of It)
date_evidence: June 23, 2026 | meta-date: 2026-06-23T00:00:00Z; On June 2, 2026, the Office of the United States Trade Representative issued a press release announcing affirmative determinations in all 60 of its Section 301 forced labor investigations
key_claim: On 2 June 2026 USTR made affirmative determinations in all 60 Section 301 forced-labor investigations, covering economies that account for 99.4 percent of US goods imports, and proposed additional tariffs of 10 to 12.5 percent; the Section 122 surcharge expires 24 July 2026.
frame_summary: The administration is deploying Section 301 at unprecedented breadth to replace the struck-down IEEPA tariffs, effectively tariffing almost the entire import base and entrenching coercion as the default trade tool.
signals_supported: US tariff regime after the IEEPA ruling
verbatim_quote: The 60 economies collectively account for 99.4% of all goods imported into the United States. The USTR has proposed additional tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on imports.

title: Trade Policy Shifts: IEEPA Tariffs End, Section 122 Begins, and Sections 301 and 232 Activity Grows
date_evidence: Originally published on February 23, 2026; Updated on March 5, 2026 | a 10 percent tariff which was raised to 15 percent the following day under Section 122 ... 150 days until July 24, 2026
key_claim: The Section 122 surcharge was set at 15 percent for 150 days from 24 February to 24 July 2026, and USTR confirmed multiple new Section 301 investigations on an accelerated timeframe covering overcapacity, forced labor, digital services taxes and more.
frame_summary: With IEEPA tariffs invalidated, the administration is systematically substituting Section 122 and a wave of accelerated Section 301 and 232 actions, keeping the tariff architecture largely intact.
signals_supported: US tariff regime after the IEEPA ruling
verbatim_quote: These tariffs take effect February 24, 2026, and will remain in place for 150 days – until July 24, 2026 – unless extended by an act of Congress.

title: CIPS volumes rise as China expands payments infrastructure
date_evidence: Joe Baker 19 June, 2026 | in April broke its record for single-day transaction value, with RMB 1.22tn ($178.5bn) passing through the system
key_claim: CIPS broke its single-day record with RMB 1.22tn ($178.5bn), reached 1,791 participating institutions by end-Q1 2026, and had a March average daily volume of RMB 920.5bn up 20 percent year on year, though the yuan is still under 3 percent of SWIFT payments versus 51 percent for the dollar.
frame_summary: China's CIPS is scaling into a genuinely large yuan-settlement rail, boosted by Middle East oil demand, but still depends on SWIFT and remains far smaller, so it erodes the dollar order at the edges rather than displacing it.
